newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING-DERBY WINNER DRAWS NUMBER SEVEN POST FOR PREAKNESS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DERBY WINNER DRAWS NUMBER SEVEN POST FOR PREAKNESS.

text.p: Kentucky Derby winner Silver Charm on Wednesday drew the seventh post position in a 10-horse field for Saturday's 122nd running of the Preakness Stakes and was immediately installed as the 9-5 favourite.

Captain Bodgit, who finished a very close second to Silver Charm at Churchill Downs, drew the ninth position for the middle leg of thoroughbred horse racing's Triple Crown and was made second favourite at 2-1.
The inside position went to 50-1 longshot Jack at the Bank, while Free House, who finished third in the Derby, drew the desirable fourth position and 9-2 odds.
Free House will have a new jockey for the Preakness -- Kent Desormeaux, who replaces David Flores.
Silver Charm turned in a strong 1 1/2-mile workout at Pimlico Wednesday, according to trainer Bob Baffert, who said he was reasonably pleased with the gate from which jockey Gary Stevens will break.
"I just didn't want to be inside or dead on the far outside," Baffert said. "There's a lot of speed sitting inside of us, so Gary can see what he wants to do.
"He's still training good so I'll tell Gary he's got a lot of buttons to push," added Baffert.
Baffert said he didn't expect Silver Charm would be able to run quite as strong a race as he did in Kentucky two weeks ago, but he was not concerned.
"I expect him to take a step back, but Captain Bodgit should take a step back, too."
Captain Bodgit trainer Gary Capuano said he would have preferred a post position further inside.
"At Pimlico, inside is better," he said. "It's always best to be inside, mainly because of the tight turns."
But he added: "It's a mile and three sixteenths race, so there is plenty of time for them to sort themselves out."
Capuano said his horse would likely stick with its usual come-from-behind strategy despite the difficulty the Pimlico track presents.
"This track has always been a little harder to close on than some others, but they can do it."
Of the six three-year-olds in the field who did not run in the Kentucky Derby, the strongest contender looks to be Lexington Derby winner Touch Gold, who drew the fifth post and was listed at 5-1.
Touch Gold will be ridden by veteran jockey Chris McCarron, who missed the Derby with a shoulder injury.
George Steinbrenner, as he has done so often with his New York Yankees managers, fired jockey Carlos Marquez Jr. and will have Mike Smith on his horse, Concerto.
Concerto, which faded to ninth in the Derby, will break from the sixth gate and was listed at 12-1 odds.
Smith will ride Concerto for the first time in a race on Saturday.
